meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone hear from him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. And you still haven't told me whether anyone heard from Owen before the zero.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Print that history and send it to me tonight. What else do you have, Hale?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote all the time; that could be a different edition or a line he got wrong.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll check that line myself. Whatever comes of this, it stays off Owen's record and it stays out of his classroom.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their minds between an outline and an essay.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, private, and before December 1. Owen will do the rewrite to put this behind him, and I want your email tonight saying nothing goes on his file. That changes nothing about what I think of how this started.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. Put the time and the room in that email, and I'll make sure he's there.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay under procedure 4.4, after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in his record. I still require that commitment in writing, with the time and room for the rewrite, and I have not changed my view of how the zero was entered. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 after school; she still wants your written confirmation tonight, with the time and room, that the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You turned the screen and showed the version history with its exact late-night times, because it was dated, specific, tied to Owen's own file, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing lost ground outright, but you never answered whether anyone spoke with Owen before the zero went in, and that open question will come back to you.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed close to that, a burst of writing just before midnight the night before the essay was due, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she pushed so hard on procedure.
Try next time: Right after owning the zero, answer her first question directly by saying whether you spoke with Owen before entering the mark, since procedure 4.1 makes that the first step and she was clearly building toward it.
